headline: Character AI files for Chapter 11, lines up Disney as bidder
dek: The chatbot startup listed up to $100 million in liabilities and accepted Disney as lead bidder, per The Verge and Engadget.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Chapter 11 to clear a sale
body: Character AI, the startup where users chat with chatbot characters, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US to facilitate a sale of the company (The Verge, Engadget).
Disney was accepted as the lead bidder and offered $20 million for unspecified assets. The figure could rise if other bidders offer more (The Verge, Engadget).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the auction works
s3.body: In Chapter 11, assets are typically sold in a court-supervised auction. Disney's opening bid sets the price floor (The Verge, Engadget).

points.t: Disney is the stalking horse, whose offer sets a baseline for rival bidders (The Verge, Engadget).
Character AI listed between $50 million and $100 million in estimated liabilities (The Verge, Engadget).
Disney would help with the transition using staff it already hired away from Character AI (The Verge, Engadget).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A rival turned buyer
body: Disney had sent cease-and-desist letters over unauthorized chatbots built on its characters. It still hired former CEO Karandeep Anand as its chief technology officer (The Verge, Engadget).
In 2024, Google spent more than $2 billion to hire much of the team, including co-founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas (The Verge, Engadget).

stat.cap: Disney's opening bid for unspecified assets

items.t: The company plans to keep services and paid subscriptions running during the sale (The Verge, Engadget).
A court-approved sale is expected between late November and early December (The Verge, Engadget).
If no suitable buyer is found, the platform could be shut down (The Verge, Engadget).

caption.hook: Character AI filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US and lined up Disney as the lead bidder, with a $20 million offer.
body: According to The Verge and Engadget, the startup listed estimated liabilities of $50 million to $100 million. Disney's bid is the opening offer in the auction and could rise if others bid higher.

The company says it will keep services running, including paid subscriptions, while the sale is pending, expected between late November and early December. If no suitable buyer is found, the platform could be shut down.
